# ezghcloud_hosted_queue_rabbitmq_queue (Resource)

A queue on a RabbitMQ cluster. New queues are quorum queues unless the app declares another type. Destroying it deletes this queue and its messages, nothing else; queues apps declare are never touched unless imported.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster (hqc_) it is in. Changing it replaces the object.
- `name` (String) The queue's name. Changing it replaces the object.
- `project_id` (String) Project of the cluster. Changing it replaces the object.
- `vhost` (String) The vhost it is in: / (or default) for the default vhost. Changing it replaces the object.

### Optional

- `arguments` (String) Arguments as a JSON object (jsonencode), at most 32 entries. Changing them replaces the object.
- `durable` (Boolean) Whether the queue survives a broker restart. Changing it replaces the queue.
- `type` (String) quorum, classic or stream; the vhost's default_queue_type when left out. Changing it replaces the queue.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) cluster_id/name, with the vhost before the name for a RabbitMQ object.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `origin` (String) api if it was made through EZGH, broker if an app made it first (an imported object).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_hosted_queue_rabbitmq_queue.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/CLUSTER_ID/VHOST/NAME'
```
